shots.featureName: Orient yourself in Microsoft Foundry
shots.caption: The New Foundry toggle in the portal header
shots.alt: The Microsoft Foundry portal header with the New Foundry toggle switched on and the project name in the upper-left corner, which shows you are in the new portal.
shots.navHint: Start on the Microsoft Foundry portal, signed in, with the New Foundry toggle on.
setup: Sign in to Microsoft Foundry at https://ai.azure.com with the Azure account you will use for the labs.
Make sure the New Foundry toggle is on. These labs, unless they say otherwise, use Foundry (new) and Foundry projects.
Find the project name in the upper-left corner. If you have no project yet, you create one in the next lab.
Read the What you can build table in What is Microsoft Foundry? and note the three capabilities: Agents, Models, and Tools and knowledge.

Read the Start by building an agent section and decide your first build: a prompt agent (declarative, hosted by Foundry), a hosted agent (your own code in a container), or a single model call with no tools.
Open the Evolution of Foundry table and write down the current term for each previous term you know, for example Azure AI Foundry to Microsoft Foundry and Assistants API to Responses API.
Toggle New Foundry off to see the Foundry (classic) portal, note that hub-based projects live there, then turn the toggle back on.
instructions: Open https://ai.azure.com signed in.
Show the New Foundry toggle in its on position and the project name in the upper-left corner.

shots.featureName: Grant access with Foundry roles
shots.caption: Assigning the Foundry User role
shots.alt: The Azure portal Access control (IAM) role assignment flow for the Foundry User role with the Members step visible and a principal selected.
shots.navHint: Start in the Azure portal, signed in to the subscription you use for Foundry.
prerequisites: Create a Foundry project
setup: Choose the role and scope per persona, for example Foundry User on the project for developers and Foundry Agent Consumer for callers that only use agent endpoints.
In the Azure portal, open your Foundry resource and go to Access control (IAM).
Create a role assignment for Foundry User, set Members to User, group, or service principal, select the principal, and select Review + assign.
Repeat with Members set to Managed identity and select your project's managed identity.
Alternatively in the Foundry portal, select Manage > Project details, open the Users tab, select Add user, enter the email address, and select Add.
If users need quota visibility, assign Cognitive Services Usages Reader at the subscription scope.
Use role definition IDs instead of names in scripts because of the role rename; Foundry User is 53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d.

shots.caption: A Foundry estimate in the pricing calculator
shots.alt: The Azure pricing calculator with two Foundry-related services added and the estimate summary visible, which is the baseline you compare to real charges.

setup: Confirm you have Cost Management Reader and Foundry User at the subscription or resource group scope.

shots.featureName: Create a prompt agent with Foundry Agent Service
shots.caption: The agent quickstart output
shots.alt: A terminal showing the new agent's ID, name, and version, followed by an answer to a follow-up question that reflects the earlier question.
shots.navHint: Open your Foundry project (set CAPTURE_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_URL to its address), then follow the setup steps. If a step runs in a terminal, capture the terminal with an OS screenshot tool and save it at the planned filename.
prerequisites: Create a Foundry project
Deploy a model and test it in the playground
setup: Make sure you have a Foundry project, a deployed model (for example gpt-5-mini), and Application Insights connected to the project.
Run pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0" and sign in with az login.
Copy the project endpoint from the project welcome screen; it has the form https://<resource-name>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<project-name>.
In your script, set the project endpoint and an agent name, and create an AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential.
Call project.agents.create_version with a PromptAgentDefinition that sets the model and the instructions.
Get an agent-bound client with project.get_openai_client(agent_name=...) and create a conversation.
Call openai.responses.create with the conversation ID and a question, then send a related follow-up in the same conversation.
When finished, delete the resource group in the Azure portal if you no longer need the resources.
instructions: Run the quickstart script in a terminal.
Show the printed agent ID, name, and version, and the follow-up answer that reflects the first question.

prerequisites: Create a prompt agent with Foundry Agent Service
setup: Create a small text or Markdown file that contains a fact a model could not know, such as an invented product detail.
Confirm the Foundry User role on the project and the Storage Blob Data Contributor role on the project's storage account, then run pip install azure-ai-projects and sign in with az login.
Copy the project endpoint from the project welcome screen and set it in your script with a model deployment name.
Create an AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential and get the OpenAI client with project.get_openai_client().
Create a vector store with openai.vector_stores.create, then upload your file with openai.vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll so ingestion finishes before you query.
Create an agent version with project.agents.create_version and a PromptAgentDefinition whose tools include FileSearchTool(vector_store_ids=[vector_store.id]).
Create a conversation and call openai.responses.create with an agent_reference for your agent and a question only the file can answer.
Compare the answer to the file, then delete the agent version and the vector store with project.agents.delete_version and openai.vector_stores.delete.
instructions: Run the file search script.
Show the question and the grounded answer printed in the terminal.

prerequisites: Create a prompt agent with Foundry Agent Service
setup: Grant the Foundry User role on your project to the developer identity, and to the agent identity if you use a prompt agent.
Install the SDK with pip install azure-ai-projects and create an AIProjectClient with your project endpoint and DefaultAzureCredential.

Call project.toolboxes.create_version with a toolbox name, a description, and tools such as WebSearchToolboxTool(), an MCPToolboxTool with a server_label, server_url, and project_connection_id, and ToolSearchToolboxTool().
Note that the first version you create is promoted to the default version automatically.

Install an MCP client with pip install mcp, connect to the version-specific endpoint with a token for https://ai.azure.com/.default, and call list_tools.
Confirm the expected tool names appear, remembering that MCP tool names are prefixed with the server_label.
Attach the consumer endpoint to an agent as an MCP tool, run one request that uses a toolbox tool, and promote later versions to default when you are ready.

shots.featureName: Troubleshoot publishing and published agents
shots.caption: A publish validation error
shots.alt: The publish dialog showing a validation error message that names the field to correct, such as an invalid app version.
shots.navHint: Open your agent in your Foundry project (set CAPTURE_FOUNDRY_PROJECT_URL to the project address), then follow the setup steps to Publish.
prerequisites: Publish a Foundry agent to Microsoft Copilot and Teams
setup: Read the exact error text from the publish dialog or the API response and find its row in the Resolve publishing issues table.
For a validation error, fix the field the message names, for example change the version to digits and periods only, and publish again. If the app version already exists, increment it.
If Download ZIP returns no package, correct the field named in the error and retry; Foundry does not return a package that fails manifest validation.

If you see 403 AuthorizationFailed for Microsoft.BotService/botServices/write, assign the Azure Bot Service Contributor Role, Contributor, or Owner on the resource group, refresh your credentials, and retry.
If the agent is missing from the store, check the publish scope, confirm admin approval in the Microsoft 365 admin center for organization scope, then clear the store cache or sign out and back in.
If the agent works in the playground but fails once published, assign the required roles to the agent's identity for each Azure resource it accesses, and check that the agent identity is enabled.
If the conversation is stuck or returns no tool output found, reset it with a new chat in Microsoft Copilot or /foundry_new_preview in Teams.
If users get an insufficient permissions error, check that the user has permission to invoke the agent endpoint under BotServiceRbac.
instructions: In the publish dialog, enter an invalid version such as one that starts with 0 and select Publish.
Show the validation error message. Revert the field afterward.

prerequisites: Create a prompt agent with Foundry Agent Service
Publish a Foundry agent to Microsoft Copilot and Teams
setup: Confirm you have a Foundry agent from the new portal, its Agent ID, the project's Azure AI Project endpoint, and a primary Copilot Studio agent built with the Microsoft Copilot harness.

Enable the Activity protocol by publishing the Foundry agent to Microsoft 365 or Teams, or by calling the Foundry Agents - Update agent REST API to set protocols to responses and activity and add the BotServiceRbac scheme. Keep responses and Entra in the lists.
Sign in to Copilot Studio at https://copilotstudio.com, open the primary agent, and select the Build tab.
In the components panel, select Connected agents, select Add, and then select Add Foundry agent.
On Connect to Azure AI Foundry, pick an existing Connection, or select Create new connection, enter the Azure AI Project Endpoint, and select Create, then Next.
On Review and add, enter a Name, a specific Description, and the Agent ID, then select Add to agent.
Confirm the agent appears under Connected agents in the components panel.
Select the Preview tab, send a message in the Foundry agent's domain and one outside it, and check that only the first is answered by the Foundry agent.
